knowledge_point.title: Separating a Logarithm Into Two Logarithms Using the Quotient Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's recall the quotient rule for natural logarithms:

$$
\ln(a)-\ln(b)=\ln(\frac{a}{b})
$$

Using the quotient rule for natural logarithms, the given expression can be rewritten as:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln(\frac{14}{e^{4}}) &= \ln(14)-\ln(e^{4}) \\ &= \ln(14)-4\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: Positive real logarithm arguments; base e.
